title: I Took the Koi-Pond Feeding Log to the Chair Who Pocketed My Numbered Pellets

parts.text: I stepped into the koi deck at 7:04 a.m. and chair Mei was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE FEED. TEN MINUTES. PELLETS STAY WITH THE LOG. I was thirty-two, garden secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our numbered pellets. Mei shrugged. "Chairs are the pond." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover scoop on my numbered pellets. Then I asked for the feed log. At 7:12 the shed pinged why Mei's name was on my scoop. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shed can see Mei's leftover scoop on my numbered pellets.

social.video_title: She pocketed my numbered koi pellets on my feed — Part 1/2
social.description: Koi deck, leftover scoop, a ten-minute clock she posted. I logged the pellets. Would you have asked for the feed log?

parts.text: Mei called it extra protein until the shed asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the scoop still. The pellets went back to my numbered log. Mei ran a slot of her own and told the next chair atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE POND. I keep my pellets in a labeled bin. Mei brown-bags her protein. The deck finally looks like a log, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Chairs are not the pond — Part 2/2
social.description: Feed log, numbered pellets, and a second line on the board. Was extra protein ever my scoop?
